stories.title: How aquanauts could help save Florida’s reefs
stories.summary: An underwater habitat, Vanguard, deployed in the Florida Keys, is enabling aquanauts to monitor coral restoration efforts around the clock. Corals stressed by warmer surface waters were relocated to a deeper, cooler nursery next to Vanguard, where they are beginning to recover. This approach allows continuous observation of marine life, including urchins crucial for reef health.

stories.significance: Long-stay underwater habitats allow continuous day and night marine research without the strict time limits and decompression restrictions of boat-based diving.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: The U.S. just lost its measles elimination status. What now?
stories.summary: The U.S. has lost its measles elimination status, declared by the Pan American Health Organization on November 17, 2026, due to uninterrupted spread for over a year, with nearly 100 outbreaks, thousands sickened, and nearly a dozen deaths since 2025. Regaining status requires stopping outbreaks and proving no local transmission for a full year, primarily through increased vaccination.
stories.finding: The U.S. has lost its measles elimination status, declared by the Pan American Health Organization on November 17, 2026, due to uninterrupted spread for over a year, with nearly 100 outbreaks, thousands sickened, and nearly a dozen deaths since 2025. Regaining status requires stopping outbreaks and proving no local transmission for a full year, primarily through increased vaccination.
stories.significance: Losing measles elimination status marks a significant reversal of decades of public health progress and underscores risks stemming from declining vaccination coverage.
stories.caveat: Underreporting and untested cases hamper accurate surveillance, making the true scope of outbreaks difficult to determine.
entities: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
Brown University School of Public Health

stories.title: Perseverance Update: The Ghostly Rocks of ‘Idubi’ — Bright Remnants of Aqueous Systems from Long Ago
stories.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover identified bright, silica-rich rocks in Mars' "Idubi" area, confirmed by SuperCam data to be hydrated silica. These deposits, which can preserve microfossils on Earth, suggest ancient Martian aqueous systems and are now undergoing detailed proximity science investigations to understand their origin and biosignature preservation potential.
stories.finding: NASA's Perseverance rover identified bright, silica-rich rocks in Mars' "Idubi" area, confirmed by SuperCam data to be hydrated silica. These deposits, which can preserve microfossils on Earth, suggest ancient Martian aqueous systems and are now undergoing detailed proximity science investigations to understand their origin and biosignature preservation potential.
stories.significance: Hydrated silica forms in aqueous settings that may support habitability and possesses strong potential for preserving microfossils and biosignatures.
stories.caveat: High-resolution chemical and mineralogical proximity science data are still being gathered to constrain the rocks' exact origin and biosignature preservation potential.

stories.title: Nuclear bomb in space would disable 98 per cent of satellites within a week
stories.summary: A new model suggests a single 1-megaton nuclear explosion 500 km above the South Atlantic could disable 98% of satellites within a week, even with radiation-hardened chips. The primary damage comes from electrons trapped in Earth's magnetic field, creating an artificial radiation belt. Recovery could take years due to elevated radiation and increased debris, risking Kessler syndrome.

stories.significance: A single exoatmospheric nuclear detonation could disrupt modern critical space infrastructure like GPS and communications, triggering collisions and prolonged societal degradation.

stories.title: What Makes Up the Cosmos? A 20-Year Survey Hints That Something Is Missing.
stories.summary: The Dark Energy Survey's final results, combined with data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, suggest the standard model of cosmology (Lambda-CDM) is incomplete. The findings indicate a "three-sigma" preference for a theory where dark energy is not stable and has weakened over time, though this falls short of the "five-sigma" confidence needed for a new discovery.
stories.finding: The Dark Energy Survey's final results, combined with data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, suggest the standard model of cosmology (Lambda-CDM) is incomplete. The findings indicate a "three-sigma" preference for a theory where dark energy is not stable and has weakened over time, though this falls short of the "five-sigma" confidence needed for a new discovery.
stories.significance: The finding challenges the standard Lambda-CDM cosmological model, hinting that the prevailing understanding of the universe's primary energetic component is incomplete.
stories.caveat: Preprint / working paper; peer review is not established. The observed statistical preference is three-sigma, falling short of the five-sigma threshold physicists require to claim a definitive new discovery.
